newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand shares close weaker on light volumes.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand shares close weaker on light volumes.

text.p: * NZ shares end weaker, but volumes very light
* Rumours circulate of a placement of Air NZ B shares
* Dow volatility overhangs NZ equities
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
310 -6 * NZSC cap index -7.53 at 5,043.70
345 -4 * Volume NZ$30 million. June futures untraded
635 -8 * Other movers - +5 -15
New Zealand shares closed weaker on Tuesday, but brokers stressed the 21.77-point fall in the top-40 index was on very light volume of just NZ$30 million.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended the day at 2,217.06, with Telecom down eight cents at $6.35.
Vicky St John, broker at First NZ Capital, said while Telecom had accounted for a resonable portion of the index's fall, the weakness was across the board.
Carter Holt Harvey shed six cents to $3.10, Lion Nathan was down three at $3.46 and Brierley Investments lost one to $1.33.
St John said now that the major companies had reported their half-year results, there was little to stimulate the market, and recent volatility on Wall Street was not helping matters.
"That overhangs us a little bit, that volatility in the Dow," St John said. "So there's nothing really at this stage to halt the lacklustre trading (in New Zealand)."
Brokers said rumours of a placement of Air New Zealand B shares were responsible for the stock's seven cent decline to $3.90.
"Air New Zealand Bs came off because there's a rumour that someone tried to do a placement of stock there," said one broker, who declined to be named.
Another broker said there were all sorts of rumours going around about the stock, but he couldn't comment because his firm was involved with one of them.
Air New Zealand A shares were down two cents at $2.70. Both the A and B shares go ex eight cent dividends on Monday next week. -- Matthew Brockett (64 4) 473-3736
